Speech chunk:
in Canada and throughout the world depends ultimately on market considerations. The Minister of Finance (Mr. Chretien) amplified on that this afternoon when he was discussing problems with relation to nickel and in particular, expectations respecting future market trends. The cyclical nature of supply and demand in the international market place plays a very important part in the decisionmaking process as to whether to develop various ore deposits and the commitment of required investments into such developments. Similarly, the rate of consumption must determine the rate of production in any given market condition, and the situation today in many mineral commodities is indeed-as we are finding with regard to nickel-one of over-supply, with massive inventories overhanging world markets. This condition is further complicated by the continuation of high production rates by some developing countries which rely heavily on their exports of metals and minerals for foreign exchange earnings.
